premeditation_planning: Yes, premeditated to murder to marry PW1
motive: To marry PW1 by murdering her husband
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence of PWs 1 and 2 regarding the motive for commission of the offence, the last seen circumstance and recovery as well as the identification of the dead body was consistent with the case of the prosecution. The superimposition test strengthened the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 regarding the identification of the body.
witness_credibility: PW1 was cross-examined at length, but the defense could not discredit her evidence on material particulars. The evidence of PW1 was fully supported by the evidence of PW2, the mother of PW1. The testimony of PW7, the Village Administrative Officer, was also relevant and significant.
trial_duration: Trial judgment: 19.03.2009; High Court decision: 19.03.2009; Supreme Court decision: 29.03.2019
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Balaji Srinivasan, AAG, Sushil Kumar, Sr. Adv., Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, K. K. Mani, Ms. T. Archana, Jaideep Singh, Aditya Kumar, S. Ratnakaran, Bhagwan Das, Thankaih, T. Gopal, Vaidruti Misra, M. Yogesh Kanna, S. Partha Sarathi, S. Raja Rajeshwaran, Ms. Pallavi Sengupta, Advs. for the appearing parties. Counsel for the State: Not explicitly stated.
investigation_status: First Information Report (FIR) lodged for abduction; separate FIR for murder; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under s.304 Part-I modified to s.302 by High Court; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeals
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused no.1 wanted to take PW1 as his third wife, knowing she was already married to the deceased, and made several attempts to sever the relationship between PW1 and her husband. The murder of the deceased was committed to marry PW1 without obstruction. The evidence of PW1 and PW2, along with the recovery of the deceased's belongings and identification of the body, supported the prosecution's case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the murder was a continuation of the earlier abduction incident and that the two events were part of the same investigation. They also challenged the reliability of the identification of the body through superimposition and DNA evidence, asserting that the absence of DNA testing made the identification improper.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that circumstantial evidence, when conclusive and consistent, can establish guilt. It also emphasized that opinion evidence, including DNA and superimposition tests, is advisory and not binding on the court.
